(This is an unserious project I did to learn some more about partial_fixpoint). Have you ever wanted to define an arithmetic sequence, but were worried that it did not depend on unsolved conjectures? Look no further than Collatz Recursion Schemes! With Collatz Recursion Schemes you only need to provide F(1), and F(n) in terms of F(3n+1) or F(n/2). If the usual recurrence equations are true, you get a program correctness statement that is equivalent to the Collatz Conjecture! 

theorem CollatzRecursionScheme.toFun_eq_extend_iff_collatz (s : CollatzRecursionScheme)
    {spec : ℕ+ → ℕ+} (Hv : s.Valid spec) : s.toFun = extend spec ↔ CollatzConjecture := ...

I have used the Collatz recursion scheme to implement the sequence 2n+1 and have tested it to sufficiently large values (50). This is clearly extremely strong evidence that the Collatz conjecture is true. I'll expect my fields medal in the mail.
